headline: Flávio Bolsonaro Leads Lula Into Brazil's October 25 Runoff
seoTitle: Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula Advance to Brazil Runoff
seoDescription: Brazil's electoral authority says Flávio Bolsonaro won 47.03% and Lula 45.16%, sending the presidential race to an October 25 runoff.
deck: The official count put Bolsonaro ahead by about 2.23 million votes, but neither candidate cleared the threshold for a first-round victory.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advanced to an October 25 presidential runoff after neither won a first-round majority. Brazil's Superior Electoral Court reported Bolsonaro at 56,104,268 votes, or 47.03%, and Lula at 53,876,617 votes, or 45.16%, with 99.99% counted.
The result reversed late pre-election polling that had generally shown Lula ahead. Reuters reported that cost of living, corruption and public security dominated voter concerns.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Both candidates now compete for voters who backed other first-round choices or cast blank and null ballots. The runoff winner will face high public debt, sluggish growth forecasts and a deeply polarized political environment.
FMB News' earliest report on the closing stage of the campaign is available at https://www.francinemariebautista.com/news/brazil-lula-flavio-bolsonaro-close-campaigns-october-3-2026/.

sections.heading: Why Filipinos should watch
paragraphs: Brazil is one of the world's largest food and commodity exporters and a major emerging-market economy. Changes in its fiscal, trade and foreign policies can affect commodity markets and broader relations among Global South economies, including the Philippines.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch endorsements from eliminated candidates, official runoff campaigning, fiscal-policy proposals, disinformation safeguards and the final October 25 count.
